entries.title: Isaiah 65:1
segments:
vv 1-2. 
 
  Them that asked not for me; the Gentiles. 
 
  A rebellious people; Israel.  See the apostle Paul's explanation of these two verses,

.  The prophet then proceeds to rebuke the Jews for their sins, and to show them that the kingdom of God shall be taken from them and given to others. 
 
Christ will always have a seed to serve him.  When the great body of the Jewish people rejected him, he took from them the kingdom of God and gave it to the Gentiles.  so will he continue to deal with every branch of his visible church that proves unfaithful to its high calling.

entries.title: Isaiah 65:3
segments:
Sacrificeth; to idols. 
 
  In gardens; which were a common resort for idolators. 
 
  Upon altars of brick; literally, "upon bricks."  Some suppose an allusion to the command given,
, that God's altars should be made of earth or unhewn stone.  But it is more probable that the bricks themselves contained images or symbols of their gods.

entries.title: Isaiah 65:4
segments:
Among the graves--in the monuments; they used sepulchral caves for their idolatrous rites.  The word rendered "monuments" rather signifies recesses, caverns in the rocky cliffs. 
 
  Eat swine's flesh; which was forbidden by the law of Moses,
, and was undoubtedly connected with idolatrous observances.

entries.title: Isaiah 65:5
segments: A smoke in my nose, a fire; they excite my wrath.  Compare

. 
 
Great wickedness and great self-righteousness are often found united in the same persons and communities.

entries.title: Isaiah 65:7
segments: When the children sanction and perpetuate the sins of their fathers, God will recompense both together into their bosom.

entries.title: Isaiah 65:8
segments:
New wine; that is, juice from which new wine can be made. 
 
  The cluster; probably a good cluster among a mass of corrupt clusters which the vintages are destroying. 
 
  A blessing is in it; God has blessed it, and thus made it valuable. here, as often elsewhere, the prophet foretells the preservation of a pious remnant amid the general destruction of the people.

vv 8-16. 
 
The same wind which blows away the chaff, cleanses the wheat and makes it ready for the garner; so the same judgments of God which destroy the wicked from among his people, purify the righteous and prepare them for a more abundant increase.

entries.title: Isaiah 65:11
segments:
Ye; the mass of the Jewish people. 
 
  That troop--that number; "Gad" and "Meni," names of false gods.

entries.title: Isaiah 65:14
segments: My servants; the true worshippers of Jehovah,

entries.title: Isaiah 65:15
segments:
Shall slay thee; the outward Israel. 
 
  His servants; the true Israel; the same as the seed which God will bring forth out of Jacob.
By another name; the church of God shall no longer be named from Israel, but from Christ, without respect to outward descent.

entries.title: Isaiah 65:17
segments: New heavens and a new earth; the new and glorious order of things under the Messiah.  There is no necessity for limiting this promise to the beginning of the Christian dispensation, or even to this world.  It includes the whole history of Christ's kingdom, to its final consummation in heaven.  Compare

. 
 
vv 17-25. 
 
Many prophets and righteous men desired to see the Redeemer's wonderful works, and to hear his words of heavenly wisdom, but died without beholding him; so they who come after us shall enjoy such manifestations of his glory as our eyes have not been permitted to witness; for the progress of his kingdom must be onward, from glory to glory, until it shall end in the everlasting light and blessedness of heaven.

entries.title: Isaiah 65:20
segments:
An infant of days; whose life is only a few days. 
 
  An old man that hath not filled his days; one who, though he has reached an advanced age, yet dies prematurely. 
 
  The child shall die a hundred years old; one who dies at that age shall be considered as dying in childhood. 
 
  The sinner being a hundred years old shall be accursed; shall be accursed by being prematurely cut off at the age of a hundred years. Compare
.  But we need not interpret the words of this verse literally.  They may be understood as a promise of great spiritual vigor under the figure of extreme longevity.

entries.title: Isaiah 65:22
segments: As the days of a tree; such as an oak, which is supposed to live a thousand years and longer.

entries.title: Isaiah 65:25
segments: The wolf--the bullock; see note on

. 
 
  Dust shall be the serpent's meat; the original curse shall be executed upon the serpent and his seed.
The kingdom of Satan shall be crushed and prostrate.
